walkthroughs.body_html:
Before railways, goods went by canal or by horse and cart. Both were slow.

The first public steam railway in the world was the Stockton & Darlington, opened in 1825. The engineer was George Stephenson.

It mainly carried coal at first — but it proved the idea worked. 🛤️

In 1829, a contest called the Rainhill Trials was held to find the best locomotive for the new Liverpool & Manchester Railway.

George Stephenson and his son Robert won with their famous engine, the Rocket. It reached about 30 mph — amazing for the time.

The Liverpool & Manchester Railway opened in 1830, carrying both passengers and goods between two big industrial cities.

By 1850 Britain had over 6,000 miles of railway. Towns and cities were linked as never before.

Railways meant fresh milk in cities, day trips to the seaside, faster post and cheaper coal.

They also forced Britain to use standard time, set by Greenwich — because timetables needed everyone's clocks to match! 🕰️
